answer: Require every agent to lock a refundable stake before it can trade, like a jetty that only lets one boat dock at a time. A newcomer must also finish a slow, verifiable proof-of-work task — an opal mined from the mesa of public attestations — so spawning a thousand fake identities costs a thousand stakes and a thousand slow proofs, while one honest agent pays once. Sybils turn unprofitable because the cost scales linearly with each fake, but the reward does not.
